lines:
Responsibilities: Dispatches an approved tool, plugin, external-agent, or whole-workspace execution into an explicitly configured container, VM, OS sandbox, or remote backend and returns verifiable enforcement and lifecycle evidence. It is optional and never the default trusted-plugin contract.
Owned runtime state: backend sessions/handles, verified image/environment identity, mount and network realization, remote workspace mapping, resource limits, cancellation handle, and artifact transfer correlation. Isolation profiles and workspace selection are pinned core inputs.
Versioned ports and contracts: IsolationBackendManifestV1, IsolationProfileV1, EnforcementClaimV1, IsolatedExecutionV1, IsolationRawEventV1, ArtifactTransferV1, and IsolationCleanupV1. Claims enumerate what the backend actually enforces, including roots/mounts, network, user identity, process limits, and residual-state policy.
Failure and degraded behavior: unavailable backend, unverifiable mount/network policy, identity drift, remote disconnect, transfer corruption, or cleanup failure is explicit. A required profile fails closed and is never downgraded to host execution; a lost remote terminal after dispatch becomes uncertain.
Security truthfulness: only a verified backend may be called a sandbox/security boundary. It cannot make an unisolated trusted plugin safe retroactively, broaden authority, select another workspace, or expose lease material beyond declared channels.
Observability, performance, and cross-platform behavior: startup/transfer/execution/cleanup metrics, content hashes, bounded streams, enforcement evidence, backend-specific health, and a consistent Aworkit port across Windows, Linux, and macOS while clearly declaring unsupported host/backend combinations.
Non-responsibilities: no default plugin security policy, capability approval, backend provisioning marketplace, canonical artifact/history storage, workflow retry, or process-supervisor authority.

data.name: Optional Isolation Backend Adapter
data.technology: Rust backend SPI for containers, VMs, OS sandboxes, and remote execution
